Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today — appreciate the context on your production footprint and regulatory needs. Quick recap + asks so we can move the security review forward: 

1) SOC 2: can you confirm whether you need a SOC 2 Type II report (full coverage) or a SOC 2 bridge letter/attestation will suffice for initial procurement? If Type II, which periods matter for you (most customers accept last 12 months).

3) Vendor security questionnaire: happy to kick off the questionnaire (we can route through our security portal) — do you prefer a completed PDF or a questionnaire URL?

4) Pen test / vulnerability management: you asked for our latest pen test report and the SLA/cadence for vulnerability scanning and remediation. If you can confirm who on your security team should receive the report, I will route it over (we typically provide a redacted vendor report and a full copy under an NDA).

Next steps I propose: I’ll loop in our security lead to share the pen-test summary and the vuln management SLA. Can we do a 30-min follow-up later this week to go over any gaps? My Calendly is below.

Thanks —

Hi all —

Thanks Marissa / Alex. Quick summary from Security and what we can provide today: 

Attachments we can share now (redacted for external):
- redwood-2026-06-pen-test-summary.pdf (summary + executive findings; PII redacted)
- vuln-management-SLA-2026-06.docx (one-page SLA covering cadence & SLAs)

Vulnerability management overview (short):
- Scanning cadence:
  - Automated dependency scans (Snyk): daily for new open-source findings.
  - Internal host/container scans (Tenable/Nessus): weekly.
  - External/blackbox scans (SecurityAssess): quarterly and after major infra changes.
  - Static analysis (CI): on every PR for server-side code.

- Pen tests:
  - 3rd-party full-scope pen test: annually (last completed 2026-06 by SecurityAssess).
  - Scoped external engagements: quarterly for higher-risk customers on request (additional scope/fee).

- Triage & remediation SLAs (targets):
  - Initial triage: within 24 hours of a confirmed finding.
  - Critical (CVSS >= 9 / RCE with exploit): patch or mitigation within 72 hours and permanent fix within 14 days where feasible.
  - High: mitigation/workaround within 14 days; remediation within 30 days.
  - Medium: remediation within 30–60 days depending on risk and business cycles.
  - Low: remediation within 90 days.

- Disclosure policy:
  - Coordinated disclosure with impacted parties; public disclosure only after remediation or after a 30-day coordination window.
  - For customer-impacting incidents, we notify affected customers within 48 hours of detection and provide a public postmortem where appropriate.

- Reporting & evidence:
  - We can provide the redacted pen-test report plus the raw finding tracker (redacted) under an NDA.
  - SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II with a 12-month coverage window; we can provide the report under standard procurement controls (we typically provide a redacted copy initially and the full report under an NDA).

Links / next steps:
- Redacted pen-test & SLA: https://drive.google.com/redwood/pen-test-2026 (link above).
- If you want the full report, please send an NDA to security@redwood.ai or request via DocuSign and we’ll route the full artifacts.

Happy to join Wednesday 8/12 at 10 PT — Marissa, please confirm the calendar invite.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
